BILL NUMBER:  S1881

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the public service law, in relation to rates charged
religious bodies and community residence supportive living facilities


 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :
This bill would clarify that not-for-profit religious organizations,
veterans organizations and supportive living facilities are already
entitled to the lowest residential rate available, by allowing them to
opt out of time of use rates.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :
This bill would allow religious organizations, veterans organizations
and community residence supportive living facilities to choose whether
they wish to be billed at a residential rate which varies with the
time of use or at the conventional single rate which does not vary
with the time of use. This legislation would amend Section 76 of the
Public Service Law.

 JUSTIFICATION :
Currently, religious organizations, veterans organizations and
community residence supportive living facilities are entitled to
receive the lowest available gas  and electric rates.   This existing
electric rate is based on single-phase residential service, regardless
of whether the religious facility actually receives single-phase or
three-phase service.  Normally, three-phase service would be billed at
a commercial rate. Time of use rates are proposed to reduce the
electric use by charging a higher rate for use during peak hours and
charging a discount rate for use during off-peak hours.  Typical
residential customers benefit from this type of proposal by shifting
their electric use to off-peak hours. However, houses of worship,
churches, religious schools and other religious organizations all of
which must operate during peak hours, do not have the option of
shifting their electric use to non-peak hours.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
1998 - A9300 - referred to corporations, authorities and commissions.
2000 - A5441 - referred to corporations.
2002 - A2259 - referred to corporations.
2004 - A6573 - referred to corporations.
2006 - S4635 - referred to energy & telecommunications.
2008 - S2290 - referred to energy & telecommunications.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
Immediately.

summary: Provides that in the event the rates charged by a utility for domestic consumers are based upon time of use, then religious bodies, associates or community residence may elect to be exempt from such time of use rates and may instead elect to be billed for its usage of such service at conventional rates that do not vary with time of use.
title: Authorizes election by religious bodies of exemption from time of use utility service rates
